title: applied-ml-experiment-scratchpad-2026-03-04-liam
content:
Daily scratchpad - quick notes, experiment queue, and TODOs

Date: 2026-03-04
Owner: Liam Chen
Context: follow-up from last week's quant experiments (int8 / q4f16) and the prompt-sensitivity eval for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) baseline. Rapid notes so I don't forget steps.

Goals for today:
- Run full eval on q4f16 variant (model: redwood/open-rl-7b) across prompt set A (50 queries).
- Re-run tokenization check for long prompts (>1024) to ensure no truncation artifacts.
- Test prefix-KV cache hit rate with batching=16, max_tokens=512.
- Write short summary for the team sync (tomorrow).

Experiment queue (high priority):
1) q4f16 run - baseline vs q4f16:
   - model: open-rl-7b@v1.3
   - quant: q4f16 with per-channel scales (from last script)
   - decode: greedy then top-k(50) for sampling comparison
   - eval set: prompt_set_A (50 queries, mix of code+instructions)
   - metrics: exact-match, ROUGE-L, and human-flag count (sampled 10)
   - notes: previous run had slight repetition on code completions -> check temperature effect

2) Prompt sensitivity sweep (short):
   - prompt_set_A variations: add one-shot example vs zero-shot; rephrase instructions (concise vs verbose)
   - measure: change in EM and length of outputs; flag hallucinations manually for 10 cases

3) KV cache + batching test:
   - infra: local-dedicated dev node (4x A100), runner script: bench_run_v3.py
   - params: batching=1,4,8,16; cache_enabled=true/false; prefix_lengths=64,128,256
   - track: avg latency/token, P50/P95, throughput (tokens/sec), cache hit ratio

Quick logs / commands to re-run (copy-paste):
- python scripts/run_quant_eval.py --model open-rl-7b --quant q4f16 --prompts data/prompt_set_A.json --out results/q4f16-run-2026-03-04.json
- python infra/bench_run_v3.py --model open-rl-7b --batch 16 --cache true --max_tokens 512 --out bench/qv16-batch16.json

Preliminary observations from yesterday (partial runs):
- q4f16 decode seems ~1.8x faster than fp16 on our dev node, memory down ~40%.
- Spot check: for prompt #12 (code rewrite), q4f16 produced syntactically valid but incorrect helper function (logic error). Marked for human review.
- Tokenization: one long prompt got trimmed; need to patch tokenizer to use truncation='none' and explicit chunking for eval set.

Open questions / TODOs (blocking):
- [ ] Confirm whether per-channel scales are being applied at matmul level or fused kernel (ask infra: @Jordan). Potential accuracy diff if scaling applied differently.
- [ ] Add a small fuzz test to catch tokenization truncation silently dropping context.
- [ ] Decide sampling temp for comparison: 0.0 vs 0.7? For deterministic eval, use greedy but also keep sampling curve.

Notes for team sync:
- Quick status: q4f16 candidate promising on perf/cost but need spot-checks for correctness regressions (sampling examples prepared).
- Request: infra help to run larger batch test on dedicated staging for stable P95 numbers.
- Ask applied-ml to prioritize 20 human-review cases from prompt_set_A to validate generation quality before broader rollout.

Scratch ideas / future experiments:
- Try mixed-precision: q4f16 for attention + fp16 for FFN (if runtime supports) - hypothesize better quality vs pure q4f16.
- Evaluate post-quantization calibration: small calibration set to re-scale outputs for logits stability.
- Build quick dashboard to show per-prompt delta between baseline and quantized variant (EM, length, hallucination flag) - useful for product sign-off.

Links / refs for later:
- GH PR (optimize): https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/412 (quant kernels + fallback)
- Confluence eval page: applied-ml/evals-2026 (design + datasets)

Random notes to self:
- Remember to push results to results/q4f16-run-2026-03-04.json and notify Asha for human review.
- If time: run one-shot prompt set to check few-shot stability.

End of scratchpad.
